concept.name: Fear of missing out
concept.definition: The apprehension that others are having rewarding experiences or opportunities one is absent from, coupled with a drive to stay continually connected; the term was popularized by Patrick McGinnis in 2004 and studied psychologically by Przybylski and colleagues (2013). In trading it manifests as chasing fast-moving assets to avoid the regret of missing gains, a dynamic exploited in pump-and-dump schemes.
concept.intuition: Watching an asset triple while strangers post profits online creates an itch to buy at any price - the pain of missing out outweighs the fear of loss.
concept.mechanics: FOMO is linked to unmet psychological needs and amplified by social media's real-time display of others' gains; in markets it drives late entries into extended moves, size inflation, and abandonment of entry criteria, and it is deliberately triggered by promoters running coordinated pumps.
concept.failure_modes: It systematically produces buying near local tops, because emotional pressure peaks exactly when a move is most extended and most visible. It also degrades selectivity, replacing setup quality with urgency.
concept.misconceptions: FOMO is not a rational response to genuine opportunity; the feeling scales with the social visibility of others' gains, not with expected value. Sitting out a move in which one had no edge is not a loss.
concept.example: After a stock doubles in a week and dominates his feed, a trader with no prior thesis buys at the high; the stock mean-reverts 30% the following week.
